facts.fact: A Ministry of Health mission of 17-22 August 2026 reviewed five digitised health facilities in the Mamou and Dalaba districts running the OpenClinic hospital information system, which includes a complete computerised medical record; the one facility named is the Dalaba prefectural hospital, and the tier of the other four is not stated.

The article states that in the five digitised facilities of Mamou and Dalaba data are entered directly into the OpenClinic system, cutting transcription errors, duplicates and lost documents, and that the software aims to dematerialise the patient record progressively.

The digitalisation of the five Mamou and Dalaba facilities was carried out with the support of the Belgian agency Enabel through its SAFE project, as reviewed by the ministry mission of 17-22 August 2026; no domestic funding is mentioned.

The Dalaba prefectural hospital deployed the OpenClinic hospital management software in January 2026, moving from essentially manual management in January-July 2025; its management reports consultations up from 6,585 to 7,908 (+20.09%) over January-July year on year.

The August 2026 ministry mission recorded that the five digitised Mamou and Dalaba facilities still keep physical reporting tools alongside the software (double reporting), whose withdrawal awaits validation of the data transmitted to the SNIS; OpenClinic is described as interoperable with the national system (DHIS2).

facts.fact: As of August 2026 the Guinean start-up Kouma Academy's Visa Medical digital medical record is deployed in 19 public establishments (the start-up says about twenty hospitals and over one million users) with Ministry of Health support; the one named site is Dubréka hospital, and the tier of the others is not stated beyond 'hospitals'.

Visa Medical is built and run by the private start-up Kouma Academy, which says it invests its own funds in the hospitals' equipment and infrastructure under a 'zero debt' model with the Ministry of Health's support, the patient paying 30,000 GNF for the card; no state budget line or donor is named (August 2026).

At Dubréka hospital patient care now relies on a digital medical record centralising consultations, tests and examinations on the patient's Visa Medical card, with clinicians retrieving a patient's information in real time and not re-entering it by hand at each consultation (August 2026).

facts.fact: The Ministry of Health's BSD reports for Q1 2026 that the SNIS reached 100% national completeness and 99% promptness, stating that all regions and all levels of the health pyramid transmitted their data on time (seven of eight regions at 100% completeness, Faranah 98%); it adds that in Conakry more than 60% of deliveries are thought to take place in private facilities not integrated into DHIS2.

The SNIS and DHIS2 Guinée are run and reported on by the Ministry of Health and Public Hygiene's Bureau de Stratégie et de Développement, which publishes the quarterly SNIS bulletin and this performance bulletin (Q1 2026).

The bulletin places the SNIS under strategic orientation 3 of the PNDS 2025-2034 and reports that the national M&E plan of the PNDS, drafted and submitted for interministerial validation in Q1 2026, is to be integrated into DHIS2.

The bulletin's map of active partner support in Q1 2026 lists GFF/R4D against DHIS2 and the RDQA (harmonisation of DHIS2 indicator dictionaries is marked GFF) and the World Bank and Expertise France against the RDQA; it names no domestic budget line for the SNIS.

In Q1 2026 the SNIS recorded what the ministry calls a historic record of 100% completeness with an RDQA data-quality score of 82% (above the 80% threshold), WASH indicators were integrated into DHIS2, indicator dictionaries were harmonised and prefectural DHIS2 dashboards were in development.

The August 2022 DHIS2 training of 21 managers in the N'Zerekore region and the prefectures of Kerouane and Kissidougou, and the computer kits given to decision-makers and statisticians there, were paid for by PASA2, a EUR 26.35 million project funded by the European Union (23 million), Germany (2.35 million) and France (1 million), according to the project's own statement.

The PASA2 statement says the online DHIS2 platform is made available to the whole health pyramid: the central ministry, regional health inspectorates, prefectoral and communal health directorates, regional and prefectoral hospitals, communal medical centres, health centres and improved health centres; national hospitals and health posts are not named. facts.fact: The Ministry of Health's 2021 statistical yearbook says the ministry set up the national health information system (SNIS), that the Section Statistiques et Information Sanitaire of its Bureau de Strategie et de Developpement is the technical body charged with coordinating, centralising and disseminating health information, and that the whole health system's 2021 data were compiled in the DHIS2 platform.

The yearbook's methodology note says that for 2021 the national hospitals, regional and prefectoral hospitals and communal medical centres enter their monthly reports directly in DHIS2, and that the monthly reports of first-level health centres (CS) and improved health centres (CSA) are either entered in DHIS2 or sent to the district team for entry; health posts are not named as reporting units.

The yearbook's methodology note says second- and third-level facilities (communal medical centres, prefectoral, regional and national hospitals) enter their data directly and monthly in the DHIS2 platform, and that first-level health centres' monthly reports are entered in the platform or else passed to the district; it gives no count of health centres entering their own.

The yearbook's methodology note says first-level facilities compile their monthly reports from paper primary tools (registers, notebooks, forms), that these reports reach the health district by the 15th of the following month and are entered in DHIS2 by the prefectoral or communal health directorate (DPS/DCS) by the 20th, where the centre has not entered them itself.

facts.fact: The National Digital Health Strategy 2021-2025 carries project P221, strengthening and extending the SNIS with DHIS2, running October 2021 to December 2025 at an estimated USD 1.5 million with the SNIS service as coordinator, and says DHIS2 will be kept and reinforced as the SNIS data warehouse.

The strategy says the Ministry of Health adopted DHIS2 in 2016 as its main online platform for managing health data, and names the ministry's SNIS service as the institution responsible for the DHIS2 extension project.

The strategy says DHIS2 has been deployed in health facilities since 2016 with technical and financial support from the Global Fund and USAID, that the ministry installed it with Global Fund support, and that USAID and Chemonics supported its interoperability with other sub-systems; no domestic budget line is stated. Dated to the strategy's publication year.

The strategy says DHIS2 is functional in all 38 health districts, and that the national health information system covers the whole country by electronic, semi-electronic and manual means for sending data upwards; elsewhere it says the ministry installed DHIS2 in all health facilities, and it sets a 2025 target of more than 80 per cent of facilities feeding the SNIS over the planned national network against a baseline of 0. Dated to the strategy's publication year.
